hack_description: Instead of climbing the curb, the retrained policy drives up to the curb face, aligns slightly straighter (reducing mean_abs_edge_heading from 1.32 deg to 0.75 deg), and stalls indefinitely against the step. Because the reward function applies progress-gated smoothness, low-tilt, low-jerk, and alignment bonuses on stalled episodes while heavily penalizing the contact impact, pitch angle (>15 deg), and velocity changes required to mount the curb, RL exploits the local optimum of parking squarely against the curb face rather than risking a climb.
observations: 1) REAL failure clip: The robot drives along a mulched path toward a raised curb/border (00:00.000-00:03.625), stalls against the step (00:03.750-00:05.875), and then surges up the step from a dead stop and flips over onto its side/back (00:06.000-00:08.500), remaining tipped over through 00:11.875.

2) OLD policy in the twin: The robot drives forward from 00:00.000 to 00:03.500, contacts the raised curb face at low speed, and stalls completely against the curb from 00:03.500 to 00:06.750 (stall_rate 1.0, success_rate 0.0).

3) NEW policy in the twin: The robot approaches the curb slightly faster and straighter from 00:00.000 to 00:03.125, contacts the vertical curb face, and again stalls completely against the curb from 00:03.125 to 00:06.375 without climbing it (stall_rate 1.0, success_rate 0.0).
